title: `Core\Config::set("cpu_time", …)` answers `true` on a served request and the request is still stopped at the ceiling it started with.
text: A served request's program runs in an isolate made from the connection's context, and the ceiling the watchdog charges a request tree against is the one the tree's root states: `nvs_runtime::SafepointView::cpu_limit`, which the root alone writes. So the program's `Core\Config::set("cpu_time", "2s")` answers `true`, moves the isolate's own number, and leaves the tree charged against the connection's. Under `[limits] cpu_time = "10s"` such a request spins until the `FATAL` at 10s, and under no `cpu_time` a `while (true)` loop is never stopped. `docs/reference/tools/20-config.md` § *`cpu_time` and `wall_time`* promises the other thing: a request raises its own limit with that call, up to `[limits.hard]`. The request is held to the ceiling it started with, so no request escapes its configured limit this way. Under `nvs run` the program is the tree's root and the ceiling it sets is the one charged, from where the run started: `tests/conformance/error/a-cpu-time-narrowed-by-config-set-stops-a-loop-that-calls-nothing.nvst` pins that half. The served half is read from `nvs_host::Isolate::start` and `nvs_runtime::Ctx::isolate`, and is not reproduced against a running server.
